observations: 4mm no-recess alignment test. Backfilled (pre-dates the logger). git_dirty: 4mm/no-recess edits uncommitted at print time. Earlier false bed-check stop = dried glue-stick residue front-left from a prior drill-template print, not a part. Printed clean. Ambient not measured.

Two-material PETG-raft splice worked end-to-end (dissimilar-material raft, per community practice): raft+brim adhered on Overture recipe; M400 U1 swap clean; PA interface gripped raft, no curl; part flat through all 20 layers at bed 70. USER VERDICT: excellent - PETG raft validated for large flat PAHT-CF. Top surface: not lifted but POROUS + mild fuzz. Filament dried to 15% RH (user-reported) pre-print - borderline for PA (want <=10%): starting moisture is prime suspect, in-print reabsorption (spool exposed through pre-warm + raft phase) secondary, top-layer speed third. Candidate fixes in order: dry to <=10%, bag spool until swap pause, slow top_surface_speed, +1-2% top flow. Ops notes: glue-ghost false positives; camera orientation corrected (image-left = printer-back). Next PA target: dual_pdm enclosure (tall - expect Z-gradient effects the flat plate avoided).

PETG-raft splice, second use (first TALL part: 20.7mm enclosure, base-down). Flat base v2 (skirt removed, no heat-shield rebate). Raft on Overture recipe; swap pause clean; PAHT-CF 290C started fine, part brim (auto_brim ~13mm) overran the 4mm raft margin ~8mm/side - sacrificial, lesson logged in filament config. CANCELLED by user at ~z2-3: slice had NO supports and roof underside (z14.2) would print as ~75mm wall-to-divider bridges - slicing miss, caught by user mid-print. Part peeled off raft clean; raft left on bed in good condition and REUSED for the follow-up job (dual_pdm_enclosure_tree row).

RESTART of dual_pdm_enclosure_flatbase on the SAME PETG raft (part-only slice Z-shifted +1.2 via shift_over_raft.py, bed_leveling=false reusing saved mesh - that mechanism WORKED: layer 1 verified laid on the raft, walls + support bases adhered, clean through layer 10). FAILED at layer ~17 (z ~3.5): organic tree supports collapsed into spaghetti across bed - detected on 15min watch, confirmed with 2nd frame, stopped. ROOT CAUSE: PA-on-PETG raft interface is deliberately weak (the release mechanism) - organic tree trunks stand on tiny dot bases with growing lever arm and nozzle-bump loads; part walls (large contiguous L1 area) held fine. LESSON: dissimilar-material raft is incompatible with skinny tree supports; use normal/grid supports (contiguous sheet bases) or model-integral sacrificial pillars anchored to the part. Raft possibly reusable again after clearing the nest.

canbox lid v6.2 letters-down on the TWICE-REUSED dual_pdm PETG raft, no brim/supports, bed 70 held throughout (incl. hours of idle hold). USER OBSERVED front corner lift early - stopped. Suspects: raft surface degraded/contaminated by two prior PA print+peel cycles over this area, and/or raft-to-plate bond letting go at the front edge after ~6h at 70C. Raft considered SPENT after two peels - lesson: one part per raft area, reuse once at most.

First run of the THIN raft (0.8mm/4 layers, sized to part +4 margin) with compressed ramp 85/78/70 - raft phase printed CLEAN and the swap+resume worked; PA base reached ~layer 20 before USER cancelled: the v6 external M6 tabs put the mount holes at 109.2mm pitch but the chassis holes are 87.5 (user's original spec; I had flagged 87.5 as superseded when the M6-tab scheme came in and proceeded without explicit confirmation - design/process miss, not a print failure). Raft undamaged at cancel time; candidate for ONE reuse if the partial base peels clean - note raft is thin (0.8) and may not survive peeling a 4mm PA slab.

Waisted canbox base attempts 2 AND 3 on the same multiply-peeled 0.8 raft. Attempt 3 stacked EVERYTHING: Z comp 0.2 (L1 at Z0.8, smashed in), half-speed L1, bed 90 full print (raft rubbery), 120s min layer time -- still did not stick (user observed). Peeled raft surface is now 0-for-4 across all mitigation combinations. Attempt 4 next per user: same settings PLUS 20mm brim on the PART, deliberately overrunning the raft edge so the brim droops to the 90C PEI and anchors from outside the raft.

COMPLETED - first canbox base to finish, and the first tall part of the whole adhesion saga. Winning recipe (attempt 2, direct on clean textured PEI, no raft): unknown-brand ASA on Generic ASA profile, 20min chamber preheat, bed 100 half-speed L1 then ramp 97/94/92/90, 15mm brim with brim_object_gap=0 (FUSED to the foot - the fix that ended the lift failures), 120s min layer time through the walls. Printer ETA was wildly pessimistic near the end (assumes remaining layers at recent-layer duration; tiny wall layers pinned to the 120s floor finish faster than projected). User pulled the part promptly. Post-checks pending: 87.5 mount pitch vs ASA shrink, M3/M6 hole fits, lid seat.

Dual-PDM v3 drill guide (204mm, enclosure-first layout): 8x M3 tap guides, 4x outer M6 tap guides, 4x 2.5 pilots for the join-ear survivors, 2x O7.3 end mounts, 36x O4.3 ringed blind chain guides around the relief pockets. Overture PETG (black) recipe with fused brim (gap 0). Done in ~100min. USER VERDICT: ok - slight lift on the +x side, worst at the front-right corner (bed x~230, y~123); brim did its job for the most part. Note for use: the guide registers on the heatsink's flush ends, so clamp it flat while drilling and a small corner bow is harmless.

Slim clamshell CANBoard enclosure, BOTH halves in one job (base upright, lid top-face-down), Generic ASA recipe with fused 15mm brims, fuzzy skin external, ramp 97/94/92/90. Clean run, no lift. Features: parting line through the O9 cable-hole centres (cradles open with the lid), lip/groove registration, wide gusseted 87.5 ears, rotated 2-line Comic Neue lid recess. Note: earlier attempt of this job in PETG died at layer 0 -- spool ran out (printer auto-paused, bed found cold); switched to ASA.

Dual-PDM v4 LEFT case (stock case skirtless, ears thickened to 8.475, join tabs cut 0.2 short of centreline, shared half-holes). ASA recipe: 100C half-speed L1, ramp to 90, 120s min layer time, 20mm brims INNER+OUTER. NO supports. USER VERDICT: FAIL (usable as a draft, only barely). Key finding: the long UNBROKEN side-to-side roof bridge (~77mm) away from the openings was surprisingly GOOD; what failed was the bridging ADJACENT to those spans: bridge lines TERMINATING IN FREE SPACE (far end landing on an opening/nothing instead of solid) drooped and wrecked those regions. Lesson: bridge-span numbers alone under-detect; per bridge region ask 'does every line end on solid material?'. Right case reprint: natural tree supports (user-approved), threshold 15deg, plate-only.

Dual-PDM v4 RIGHT case, reprint of the left-case recipe PLUS natural tree supports (user-approved after the left roof failed around its openings): SUPPORT=tree, threshold 15deg, plate-only, organic. Support audit: interface raster 5.7m at z12.4-12.6 directly under the z13.0 roof and 1.35m at z17.8-18.0 under the z18.4 surface; roof layers still FEATURE:Bridge (76.8mm lines) but land on interface. max_bridge_length=0 in profile. Chamber warm from the left-case print, no fresh soak. 103 layers, est 4h21m. USER VERDICT: great print. Tree supports (organic, plate-only, 15deg) fixed the roof: the free-space-terminating bridge lines that wrecked the left case landed on support interface this time. Recipe validated: ASA + trees on textured PEI (no raft) works.

Dual-PDM v4 LEFT case REPRINT with the tree-support recipe validated on the right case (the no-support left print failed: bridge lines terminating in free space at the roof openings). SUPPORT=tree, 15deg threshold, plate-only, organic. Interface raster 5.6m at z12.4-12.6 under the z13.0 roof, 1.3m at z17.8-18.0. 30min 100C soak before start. 103 layers, est 4h21m. USER VERDICT: good print (both tree-supported cases good). Tree-support ASA recipe now 2/2.

Dual-PDM v4 LEFT case, FINAL material: Bambu PAHT-CF, NO raft (user has printed 2x PAHT-CF raftless successfully; ASA fit-check passed first). 290C nozzle, bed 100C constant (Bambu profile default, no ramp), 20mm fused inner+outer brims, tree supports (organic, plate-only, 15deg) -- support coverage verified spatially: 100% of bridge sample points at z13.0 (8079 pts, main roof) and z18.4 (2159 pts, DT12 riser) have interface within 3mm below. Long chamber soak (bed held 100C ~1h during fit-check). USER VERDICT: success. First raftless PAHT-CF on textured PEI in the log AND first tall PAHT-CF part validated (Z-gradient concern from filament notes didn't bite). Right case next, same slice.

Dual-PDM v4 RIGHT case in Bambu PAHT-CF, identical slice to the successful left PAHT print (290C, bed 100C constant, no raft, 20mm fused inner+outer brims, organic trees plate-only 15deg, 120s layers). Start saga: two silent aborts during vibration cali (HMS 0300_1000_0002_0005, X-axis resonance; print_error 0x03004000) -- root cause likely the MISPLACED build plate rattling during the cali sweep; user power-cycled + reseated the plate, restarted with --no-vibration-cali (reusing same-day cali data) and it ran clean. USER VERDICT: great print, both halves printed super well. PAHT-CF raftless-on-textured-PEI + tree-support recipe now 2/2.

four_bolt_adaptor v7 (hex pockets 8.4 A/F). Proven spliced-raft route: PETG Overture raft (255C, bed 90 ramp 85/80/75/70, 20mm FUSED brim), M400 U1 swap pause (~45min in, as predicted), PAHT-CF plate 290C 100% infill on the 1.2 raft. Morning start per unheated-shed protocol, ~40min chamber soak from ambient ~18C. USER VERDICT: almost perfect; only minor issues on the raft-interface surface (not as smooth as printing directly on the plate) - a known cosmetic trade-off of the dissimilar-material raft. Raft route for solid plates: now 2/2.

ignition_blank v1 TEST FIT, all dims MEASURED (a26.3 b31.5 c34.5 d10 e5.9 f29.1 g4 h3, body 15 deep, tabs 4). Keyed interference plug for the cast-aluminium ignition bore: 2mm full-size land + 0.8 diametral taper (1.76deg/side), 0.2 tip chamfer, square-cornered lip. Derived: tabs STRADDLE the centre line (underside -3.74, top +6.26) per the b-span measurement, superseding the initial '5mm above CL' eyeball. Printed lip-down (zero overhangs), 30% infill, 10mm fused brim, Overture recipe 90C ramp 85/80/75/70. Purpose: verify the keyed profile + interference before any final material call.

wire_bracket rev2 (66x10x5 stadium ends r5, central 40mm wire saddle r2 fillets + 5mm lofted transitions, 2x O4 holes at 55 pitch -- clear of the wire zone, 2.5mm wall to end arcs). ASA recipe: 100C half-speed L1, ramp 97/94/92/90, 10mm fused brim, no supports (audit: zero bridges). 25 layers, ~12min.

wire_bracket rev4 (60x10x5, 35 saddle, O4.5 at 50 pitch concentric with end arcs, 100% SOLID, ASA 100C L1 ramp 97/94/92/90, 10mm fused brim). FAILED: came off the bed (user). Suspects: 100% solid infill pulls far harder than the sparse rev3 that stuck fine with the same recipe + small 10mm brim; chamber had also cycled. Reprint: identical job, chamber warm 'for ages' + bed raised to Z10 during soak. Camera note: pre-print bed checks were ONE FRAME STALE (printer serves a previously-encoded frame on connect) - fixed in camera.py this day.

wire_bracket rev4 (60x10x5, 35mm saddle, O4.5 at 50 pitch, 100% SOLID ASA, 10mm fused brim). CORRECTION of earlier 'success': completed all 25 layers but DETACHED from the bed (user). Second consecutive lift on this exact job (first: fail:lift mid-print) despite long warm chamber + raised-bed soak -- thermal-state theory DEAD. Root suspect: 100% solid ASA shrinkage on a small 60x10 footprint overwhelms a 10mm brim (sparse rev3 stuck fine). Remedy: switch to PETG Overture (low shrink) per user.

wire_bracket rev4 in PETG Overture after 2x fail:lift in 100% solid ASA (solid-infill shrinkage on a small footprint beat the 10mm brim; sparse ASA rev3 had stuck fine). Same geometry (60x10x5, 35 saddle, O4.5 at 50 pitch), 100% solid, Overture recipe: 245C, bed 90 ramp 85/80/75/70, 0.94 flow, 10mm fused brim. Fresh-frame camera check (post one-frame-stale fix): footprint + purge clear; unidentified flat object at plate REAR, outside all toolpaths.

Mid-80s Toyota dash switch mount v3 in PETG: 19x38 dash aperture, 13x18 switch hole, 23x42x2 flange, 2mm shell hollow body with a 5mm full-section block behind the clip roots, 2mm body corner radii + 1.2 lead-in chamfer, 0.4 softening elsewhere. Two opposed reverse-cantilever tabs on the ENDS, 18mm tapering 1.67->0.86, 45deg return, 1mm catch for a 2mm panel. PRINTED ON ITS SIDE so tabs flex IN-PLANE; WALLS=5; tree supports (33mm bridges at z2.4/z19.0). 15mm fused brim, bed 90 ramp 88/86/84/82, cold shed 17C ambient. USER VERDICT: great print, almost perfect. NOTE the PETG heat caveat stands for summer use (HDT 68C vs hot-car dash 69.4C) - ASA is the durable version. New slice.sh knob WALLS added for this print.

dash_switch_mount v4 (switch aperture 18.8 long, outer dims unchanged) in PETG. USER VERDICT: awesome, printed FLAWLESSLY despite the chamber DOOR LEFT OPEN on a relatively cool night -- notable data point: this recipe (on-side orientation, WALLS=5, tree supports, 15mm fused brim, bed 90 with ramp 88/86/84/82) tolerates an open door and cold ambient in PETG. Second consecutive success on this geometry.

Dash switch mount for the SECOND switch (body 6.7x18.9, flange 9.8x21.3x2.1). Same proven carrier as the rocker version (19x38 aperture, 23x42x2 flange, end snap tabs, 2mm shell); only the switch features differ: body hole 7.1x19.3 plus a 10.2x21.7 x2.1 REBATE so the switch flange sits flush with the show face. Clash-checked against a solid model of the switch: zero interference. FIT TEST only, so PETG at the user's call despite the dash HDT caveat. No soak -- printer already warm from prior prints, ambient mild. On-side orientation, WALLS=5, tree supports, 15mm fused brim.

battery_clip text-up in PAHT-CF on tree supports, REPRINT of the front-edge failure, placed --back-ymax 238 (layer1 y 163.4..248.6, ARRANGE=0 so the 219mm part was NOT auto-rotated onto Y). Completed all 125 layers; camera at finish shows the part flat and still adhered, text face up and legible, trees intact along the bar. Bed was held at 100C continuously from the previous failure through to start, so a real soak preceded it -- unlike the failed run (28C cold start). Recipe otherwise identical to the failure: 290C, bed 100 constant, 15mm fused inner+outer brims, organic trees plate-only 15deg, 120s min layer, 0.5 first-layer speed. PLACEMENT was the single variable that changed. Pending user inspection: the supported underside (the old bar top face) and how cleanly the trees release -- not judgeable from the camera. Two pads 156mm apart cannot share a brim, so they stay independently anchored; that held fine at the back of the plate.
